section_summary: This section brings together file notes, consular reports, translations, press extracts and memoranda on Japanese naval strength, operations and policy from 1931 to 1934. It covers the Shanghai fighting, naval offices and river forces in Manchuria, Pacific fortification rumors, treaty revision, and competing accounts of Japanese and American naval strategy. The final pages concern naval publicity, personnel changes and publications.

subfiles.title: File note on Japanese naval strength
subfiles.about: Points to a despatch on Japanese naval strength reported by the vernacular press.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Peck’s Nanking despatch; notes that a copy is attached.

subfiles.title: Extract on Japanese naval strength and the China crisis
subfiles.about: Reports Japanese warship numbers and Chinese political reactions to the Manchurian crisis.
subfiles.summary: The extract tabulates Japanese war vessels and displacement. It also describes the attack on China’s foreign minister, his resignation, and rumors of war or cooperation with Soviet Russia.

subfiles.title: File note on alleged Japanese naval invasion of Chapei
subfiles.about: Cross-references translations of letters from Shanghai’s mayor.
subfiles.summary: Points to Cunningham’s despatch about the alleged Japanese naval invasion of Chapei.

subfiles.title: Japanese Naval Activities
subfiles.about: Forwards the mayor’s letters about Japanese naval activity in Chapei.
subfiles.summary: Transmits two mayoral letters and a consular acknowledgment.

subfiles.title: Mayor’s letter on renewed hostilities in Chapei
subfiles.about: Protests Japanese attacks and bombardment after peace discussions.
subfiles.summary: The mayor says Japanese troops attacked Chapei despite negotiations and places responsibility on Japan.

subfiles.title: Mayor’s earlier letter on Japanese naval activity
subfiles.about: Protests Japanese naval operations in Chapei.
subfiles.summary: The mayor disputes Japanese claims and alleges an independent naval attack on Chinese territory.

subfiles.title: Consular acknowledgment to Shanghai mayor
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the mayor’s correspondence on Japanese naval activity.
subfiles.summary: Badly degraded OCR preserves only the enclosure identification and fragments of the reply.

subfiles.title: File note on Prince Fushimi’s appointment
subfiles.about: Cross-references the appointment of Prince Hiroyasu Fushimi as Navy Chief of Staff.
subfiles.summary: Points to a political report concerning the naval leadership change.

subfiles.title: Appointment of Prince Fushimi as Navy Chief of Staff
subfiles.about: Explains the political meaning attributed to a naval leadership change.
subfiles.summary: Fushimi replaces Taniguchi; observers see the change as increasing the Navy’s influence at court.

subfiles.title: File note on Japanese performance at Shanghai
subfiles.about: Cross-references observers’ unfavorable assessment of Japanese forces at Shanghai.
subfiles.summary: Notes that foreign observers considered Japan’s army and navy overrated.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on rumored Japanese Pacific fortifications
subfiles.about: Assesses a British inquiry concerning rumored Japanese bases in mandated islands.
subfiles.summary: Recommends leaving requests for information to the British Embassy in Washington.

subfiles.title: Japanese Fortifications in Pacific Insular Territories
subfiles.about: Relays a confidential English report alleging Japanese fuel, mine and base preparations.
subfiles.summary: Skinner quotes the allegation and requests instructions.

subfiles.title: Follow-up on Pacific fortification inquiry
subfiles.about: Reports renewed British interest in obtaining American information on alleged Japanese fortifications.
subfiles.summary: Cole says the English source was asked from London whether information would be forthcoming.

subfiles.title: File note on Japanese naval disarmament proposal
subfiles.about: Cross-references a report on a Japanese naval disarmament proposal.
subfiles.summary: Points to Naval Attaché Report No. 165.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Captain Sekine’s article
subfiles.about: Summarizes Sekine’s defense of Japanese naval policy.
subfiles.summary: Characterizes Sekine’s stated naval policy as defensive and notes his influence among senior officers.

subfiles.title: Extracts from Captain Sekine’s Diplomatic Review article
subfiles.about: Argues for a Japanese fleet able to defeat a naval power advancing into the Western Pacific.
subfiles.summary: Sekine describes threats he sees in Chinese resistance, foreign propaganda and misunderstanding of Japan. He defines Japan’s naval policy as defensive, favors abolishing aircraft carriers, and opposes abolishing submarines.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Japanese Naval Office in Manchuria
subfiles.about: Summarizes a report on Japan’s new naval office and coastal patrol plans in Manchuria.
subfiles.summary: Notes the office’s broad stated powers, Japanese concern over the wording, and reported orders for nine patrol boats.

subfiles.title: Forwarding despatch on Imperial Japanese Naval Office
subfiles.about: Forwards Myers’s despatch to the American Legation at Peiping.
subfiles.summary: Covering letter enclosing despatch No. 739.

subfiles.title: Imperial Japanese Naval Office in Manchuria
subfiles.about: Describes the office’s creation, leadership, powers and coastal patrol plans.
subfiles.summary: Myers reports that an imperial ordinance converted the naval mission into an office at Hsinking. He names its officers and explains Japanese officials’ concern that the ordinance openly gives it control of Manchukuo’s coasts and rivers. He also reports orders for nine patrol boats.

subfiles.title: Navy Will Establish Bureau at Hsinking
subfiles.about: Announces the Manchuria Naval Bureau and prints selected regulations.
subfiles.summary: The report names Kobayashi as commander and describes authority over coastal and river defense and local order.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Japanese naval force in North Manchuria
subfiles.about: Summarizes officers, vessels and likely Japanese control of the Sungari river force.
subfiles.summary: Nine Japanese officers are listed at Harbin. Despite claims that only Manchukuo vessels would operate, Japanese-flagged armed craft remained visible.

subfiles.title: Forwarding despatch on Japanese naval force in North Manchuria
subfiles.about: Forwards a report and officer list to the Department.
subfiles.summary: Covering letter enclosing despatch No. 2620.

subfiles.title: Japanese Naval Force in North Manchuria
subfiles.about: Reports staffing and apparent Japanese control of the Sungari naval force.
subfiles.summary: Chamberlain distinguishes two permanent Harbin Naval Office officers from seven seasonal river officers. He contrasts official claims of Manchukuo command with Japanese-flagged armed vessels and Japanese personnel observed at Harbin. He also notes brigand threats to small craft.

subfiles.title: Japanese Naval Officers Stationed in North Manchuria
subfiles.about: Lists nine Japanese officers assigned to Harbin and the Sungari force.
subfiles.summary: Names two permanent office officers and seven seasonal river-force officers.

subfiles.title: File note on New Zealand commentary about Japanese naval aspirations
subfiles.about: Cross-references an editorial on Japan and the coming naval treaty conference.
subfiles.summary: Points to a report on Japanese parity demands and the expected 1935 conference.

subfiles.title: New Zealand views on Japanese naval aspirations
subfiles.about: Reports an Auckland editorial and a traveler’s warning about Japanese naval ambitions.
subfiles.summary: The editorial anticipates Japan demanding parity at the 1935 conference. Captain Davies describes Japan’s industrial and shipping capacity and warns of a threat to Australia and New Zealand.

subfiles.title: Japanese statement on naval policy and withdrawal from the League
subfiles.about: Defends Japan’s naval preparations and links them to national policy.
subfiles.summary: The extract calls Japanese armaments defensive while allowing force against states obstructing Japanese policy.

subfiles.title: File note on Japanese naval expansion
subfiles.about: Cross-references reports of a program to reach London Treaty limits.
subfiles.summary: Notes a proposed Japanese naval expansion program.

subfiles.title: Report extract on naval expansion program
subfiles.about: Describes press reports of Japanese naval construction spending.
subfiles.summary: Reports a three-year, ¥500 million program aimed at treaty limits.

subfiles.title: File note on Japanese naval publicity in Germany
subfiles.about: Cross-references a bulletin on Japanese naval armaments and treaties.
subfiles.summary: Notes Japanese organizational publicity circulated abroad.

subfiles.title: File note on Naval General Staff Ordinance
subfiles.about: Cross-references changes in the Naval General Staff chief’s powers.
subfiles.summary: Notes expanded authority over peacetime tactics and strategic plans.

subfiles.title: Revision of Naval General Staff Ordinance
subfiles.about: Explains revised naval command responsibilities.
subfiles.summary: The revision clarifies the chief of staff’s tactical authority under the Emperor following disputes over the London Naval Treaty.

subfiles.title: File note on studies for treaty revision
subfiles.about: Cross-references Japan’s preparations for the next naval conference.
subfiles.summary: Notes appointment of a committee to study treaty issues and formulate policy.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Masanori Ito’s naval article
subfiles.about: Assesses Ito’s argument for a smaller American naval advantage over Japan.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum describes Ito as a knowledgeable naval commentator. It summarizes his view that American forces would advance toward Japan while Japanese forces would fight nearer home, and explains his fleet-ratio terminology.

subfiles.title: Comment on Ito’s account of naval strategy
subfiles.about: Challenges Ito’s description of American and Japanese naval purposes.
subfiles.summary: Argues that Japan’s navy also serves its Asian policy and that Western action might defend Western interests.

subfiles.title: Reply concerning Ito’s strategic terms
subfiles.about: Clarifies the use of offensive and defensive language in Ito’s article.
subfiles.summary: Says Ito describes defensive naval strategy regardless of a war’s cause, including conflict over China or mandated islands.

subfiles.title: Transmitting Article regarding Naval Rivalry
subfiles.about: Forwards Masanori Ito’s article on Japanese and American naval rivalry.
subfiles.summary: Grew identifies Ito as a well-connected private naval authority and highlights his moderate views.

subfiles.title: Masanori Ito’s article on Japanese and American navies
subfiles.about: Analyzes naval rivalry, construction programs and a possible Pacific war.
subfiles.summary: Ito treats the American and Japanese navies as potential opponents while favoring an agreement that each could regard as safe. He traces earlier building programs and argues that Japan must strengthen its fleet after leaving the League and amid uncertainty over its mandated islands. He compares current construction plans, depicts American strategy as offensive and Japanese strategy as defensive, and proposes a smaller American advantage to ease tensions.

subfiles.title: File note on repairs to foreign steamships
subfiles.about: Cross-references restrictions on advance repair orders at Japanese dockyards.
subfiles.summary: Suggests naval authorities wished to keep docks available for emergencies.

subfiles.title: Telegram on Japanese dockyard repair orders
subfiles.about: Reports a limit on advance repair bookings by foreign steamship companies.
subfiles.summary: Japanese dockyards reportedly could accept such orders no more than 30 days ahead.

subfiles.title: Japanese midshipmen’s practice training squadron itinerary
subfiles.about: Lists the squadron’s ports and arrival and departure dates from February to July.
subfiles.summary: Itinerary runs from Yokosuka through Asia, Europe and the Mediterranean, then back across Asia to Yokosuka.

subfiles.title: File note and extract on Japanese naval equality
subfiles.about: Records a British parliamentary answer on reports of Japanese naval parity demands.
subfiles.summary: The Lord Privy Seal had seen press reports but received no official confirmation.

subfiles.title: File note on Japanese naval policy and parity
subfiles.about: Cross-references newspaper comment on Japanese naval policy and parity demands.
subfiles.summary: Points to Colombo despatch No. 167.

subfiles.title: Japanese Navy and Politics: Rear Admiral Sakano’s Resignation
subfiles.about: Examines Sakano’s resignation amid cabinet speculation and naval politics.
subfiles.summary: The report recounts speculation over an Ugaki cabinet and Sakano’s statement that the Navy did not interfere in politics. It considers possible reasons for his removal, including internal naval disagreement, and regrets losing a moderate contact.

subfiles.title: File note on Japanese minister’s Quebec speech
subfiles.about: Cross-references a report and newspaper account of Japan’s naval policy.
subfiles.summary: Points to Randolph’s despatch on the Japanese minister’s Quebec speech.

subfiles.title: Japan Entitled to Build Up Stronger Defensive Fleet
subfiles.about: Reports Minister Tokugawa’s speech to the Quebec Military Institute.
subfiles.summary: Randolph describes Tokugawa’s friendly remarks about the United States and his discussion of Russia, Manchukuo and trade. Tokugawa argued that Japan needed a stronger defensive navy, preferably through reductions by other powers, and would seek a new accord with different ratios. Randolph adds his impressions of the speech and the circumstances of the visit.

subfiles.title: Japan’s Envoy to Canada Asserts His Nation Needs Defensive Navy
subfiles.about: Summarizes Tokugawa’s speech advocating a stronger defensive fleet.
subfiles.summary: Reports his preference for destroyers and submarines and his hope for disarmament by larger naval powers.

subfiles.title: Telegram on Japanese naval propaganda distribution
subfiles.about: Reports overseas distribution of Japanese naval publicity pamphlets.
subfiles.summary: The Navy sent 10,000 copies to societies and schools abroad and planned another 10,000.

subfiles.title: File note on Japan’s Army and Navy
subfiles.about: Cross-references a book titled Japan’s Army and Navy and translated excerpts.
subfiles.summary: Points to Donovan’s despatch No. 411.

subfiles.title: File note on Japanese naval officer changes
subfiles.about: Cross-references the Navy’s annual officer appointments.
subfiles.summary: Points to Grew’s report on the regular naval personnel shift.

subfiles.title: Annual Japanese naval officer appointments
subfiles.about: Reports changes in command of the Combined Fleet and Yokosuka Naval Station.
subfiles.summary: Names Takahashi, Suetsugu and Nagano in new posts and notes a rumor about Nagano’s conference role.

subfiles.title: New Year’s Number of Scientific Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards a Navy-themed magazine issue and translates its advertisement.
subfiles.summary: Donovan lists articles and supplements on ships, strategy, aviation and naval disarmament. He calls attention to an openly sold cruiser plan and sends copies for possible Navy Department interest.

subfiles.title: Scientific Japan advertisement
subfiles.about: Advertises the Navy-themed New Year’s issue of Scientific Japan.
subfiles.summary: Japanese-language advertisement enclosed with Donovan’s despatch.

subfiles.title: File note on prediction of a 1939 naval buildup
subfiles.about: Cross-references a Japanese Navy Department publication predicting the effects of American shipbuilding.
subfiles.summary: Points to Naval Attaché Report No. 301; its final subject line is partly illegible.
